title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
data_curation: Seed data is drawn from Open Assistant. IFT seed: 3,200 examples (first English conversational turns, human rank-0/high quality). EFT seed: built from Open Assistant's multiple ranked human responses per prompt; the SFT baseline generates chain-of-thought justifications plus a score out of 5 in the LLM-as-a-Judge format (an additive 5-point rubric over relevance, coverage, usefulness, clarity, expertise); a generated evaluation is kept only if its score ranking matches human rankings, and the set is resampled to avoid score skew (most score 4), yielding 1,630 train + 541 eval examples. Self-generated AIFT preference pairs: 3,964 for AIFT(M1)->M2 and 6,942 for AIFT(M2)->M3, formed from the highest/lowest of N=4 candidates (T=0.7, p=0.9) judged 3 times and averaged; tied-score pairs are discarded. New prompts use Self-Instruct few-shot prompting with ROUGE-L, keyword, and length filtering. Without EFT, scores collapse to 4 and only 541/429 pairs are collectible.
curriculum: Stage ordering is M0 (base Llama 2 70B) -> M1 (SFT on IFT+EFT seed) -> M2 (DPO on AIFT(M1)) -> M3 (DPO on AIFT(M2)), an Iterative DPO loop where each model generates and self-rewards the preference data training its successor; the reward model is NOT frozen and co-improves. Rationale: folding the reward model into the policy enables task transfer between judging and instruction following, lifting the human-feedback ceiling. SFT uses lr 5.5e-6 cosine-decaying to 1.1e-6, batch 16, dropout 0.1, loss on target tokens only. DPO uses lr 1e-6 decaying to 1e-7, batch 16, dropout 0.1, beta=0.1, with early stopping every 200 steps via Claude 2 pairwise AlpacaEval on 253 validation examples. Only 3 iterations are run; a positive-only SFT augmentation ablation (score-5 examples) did not help, so preference pairs were necessary.
method: Self-Rewarding Language Models make a single LLM serve simultaneously as instruction follower and as its own reward model via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting, replacing the standard frozen reward model in RLHF/RLAIF with one that updates each iteration. Self-instruction creation: generate a new prompt (Self-Instruct few-shot), sample N=4 candidate responses, and have the same model score them 0-5 with an additive five-criteria rubric (relevance, coverage, usefulness, clarity, expertise) plus chain-of-thought justification. Preference pairs (highest vs lowest scored candidate; ties discarded) train the next model with DPO (beta=0.1). Key tricks: (i) seeding the judge with EFT data so scoring doesn't collapse to one bucket; (ii) an additive rather than multiple-choice judge prompt (65.1% vs 26.6% pairwise accuracy); (iii) averaging 3 sampled judgments; (iv) judging and following share parameters for cross-task transfer. It targets the bottleneck that frozen human-trained reward models cap alignment quality.
eval_metrics: Two axes. Instruction following: GPT-4 head-to-head win/tie/loss over 256 IFT test prompts (AlpacaEval prompt, both orders, tie on disagreement); human pairwise eval (50 instructions, 3 blind annotators, majority vote); AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard win rate vs GPT-4 Turbo over 805 prompts; MT-Bench (GPT-4 grades out of 10); and 9 NLP benchmarks (ARC-Easy/Challenge, HellaSwag, SIQA, PIQA, GSM8K, MMLU, OBQA, NQ). Reward modeling: pairwise accuracy, 5-best %, exact-match %, and Spearman and Kendall tau vs human rankings on the Open Assistant eval set. Headline: AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate climbs 9.94% (M1) -> 15.38% (M2) -> 20.44% (M3), surpassing Claude 2 (17.19%), Gemini Pro (16.85%), GPT-4 0613 (15.76%). MT-Bench 6.85 -> 7.25. Reward-modeling pairwise accuracy 65.1% (SFT) -> 78.7% (M1) -> 80.4% (M2) -> 81.7% (M3); Spearman 0.253 -> 0.349. NLP benchmarks mostly hold steady (an alignment tax).
key_results: Llama 2 70B Self-Rewarding M3 reaches 20.44% AlpacaEval 2.0 win rate over GPT-4 Turbo, beating Claude 2 (17.19%), Gemini Pro (16.85%), and GPT-4 0613 (15.76%). Reward-modeling pairwise accuracy rises each iteration (65.1% SFT -> 78.7% M1 -> 80.4% M2 -> 81.7% M3), confirming the self-reward itself improves, not just instruction following. MT-Bench overall improves 6.85 (SFT) -> 7.25 (M3), and M3 beats the SFT baseline head-to-head 62.5% wins.
evolution_note: Builds on Iterative DPO / Pairwise Cringe Optimization (Xu et al.), Self-Instruct (Wang et al.), and LLM-as-a-Judge / RLAIF (Constitutional AI), but folds the reward model into the policy so it co-improves across DPO iterations rather than staying frozen -- a 2024 companion to SPIN's reward-model-free self-play. It motivates later scalable self-alignment and iterative-RLAIF work aimed at escaping the human-feedback ceiling toward superhuman agents.
